record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: Let r = (r_0, r_1, ..., r_{d-1}) be a shift radix system parameter vector, meaning that every integer sequence governed by 0 <= r_0 a_n + r_1 a_{n+1} + ... + r_{d-1} a_{n+d-1} + a_{n+d} < 1 eventually reaches the trivial all-zero cycle. The associated polynomial is x^d + r_{d-1}x^{d-1} + ... + r_0. Must every polynomial associated with a shift radix system be contractive, meaning that all of its roots have modulus less than one?

evidence.quote: The vector (r0, r1, . . . , rd−1) ∈ Rd gives a shift radix system, SRS, if the integer sequence defined by 0 ≤ r0an + r1an+1 + · · · + rd−1an+d−1 + an+d < 1 always falls into a trivial cycle 0d → 0d.
Problem 6. Must SRS polynomials be contractive ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer $d\ge 1$ and a vector $\mathbf{r}=(r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1})\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Define the map $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}:\mathbb{Z}^d\to\mathbb{Z}^d$ by
$$\tau_{\mathbf{r}}(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{d-1})=(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{d-1},-\lfloor r_0 a_0+r_1 a_1+\cdots+r_{d-1}a_{d-1}\rfloor),$$
so that the integer sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ generated by $\mathbf{r}$ satisfies
$$0\le r_0 a_n+r_1 a_{n+1}+\cdots+r_{d-1} a_{n+d-1}+a_{n+d}<1\qquad (n\ge 0).$$
The vector $\mathbf{r}$ is called a shift radix system (SRS) if, for every starting tuple $(a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1})\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, the orbit under $\tau_{\mathbf{r}}$ eventually reaches the all-zero fixed point $(0,\ldots,0)$. Associate to $\mathbf{r}$ the polynomial
$$p_{\mathbf{r}}(x)=x^d+r_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+r_1 x+r_0\in\mathbb{R}[x].$$
The polynomial $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ is called contractive if every complex root of $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ has modulus strictly less than $1$.

Question: Is it true that for every $d\ge 1$ and every shift radix system $\mathbf{r}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the associated polynomial $p_{\mathbf{r}}$ is contractive?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in surveys of shift radix systems. It is known that contractivity of $p_{\mathbf r}$ implies that every orbit of $\tau_{\mathbf r}$ is ultimately periodic (so the SRS set lies in the closure of the Schur–Cohn region), but the converse — that every SRS polynomial must have all roots inside the unit disk — appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Shift Radix Systems - A Survey (Kirschenhofer, Thuswaldner)
status_evidence.snippet: The Schur-Cohn region is the set of vectors defining a contractive polynomial; each orbit of \tau_r ends up periodically if the polynomial associated to r is contractive. Characterizing all r giving rise to an SRS remains out of range.
status_evidence.claim: Relation between contractivity and SRS property is discussed; full characterization of SRS parameters is still open.

status_evidence.title: Finite and periodic orbits of shift radix systems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on the structure of the SRS set D_d, including its relation to the Schur-Cohn region of contractive polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Open problems concerning the precise relationship between SRS parameters and contractive polynomials are stated.
